claims.statement: The European Banking Authority states that DORA became applicable on 17 January 2025 and that in-scope financial entities must maintain comprehensive registers of contractual arrangements with ICT third-party providers.
DORA requires financial entities, before entering ICT contracts, to assess criticality, risks, supervisory conditions, conflicts, and prospective-provider suitability and due diligence.
The implementing regulation defines linked templates and identifiers for contracts, entities, functions, services, and parts of the ICT supply chain, supporting a structured export use case.

contrary_evidence: DORA's legal obligation remains with financial entities, which may reject supplier-generated formats or require their own portals.
Mature GRC, trust-centre, and security-questionnaire platforms already serve overlapping workflows.
A vendor with only one regulated customer may tolerate manual diligence rather than buy another subscription.

economics.acquisition_route: Triggered referrals from ISO auditors, compliance advisers, and regulated-customer vendor portals when a diligence request is opened
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Scenario, not evidence: 1,200 vendors at PLN 18,000 annual recurring revenue yields PLN 21.6m revenue; a 40% operating margin and five mature years of distributions could create PLN 20m-plus founder net worth
economics.founder_time: Three hours per day for product and scheduled evidence review plus one hour for channel support during early cohorts
economics.gross_margin_basis: Reusable structured evidence and exports should exceed 80% gross margin; initial evidence cleanup and contract mapping reduce blended first-year margin
economics.payback: Target one to three months because onboarding is paid and channel commission is tied to the first completed room
economics.pricing: Assumption: PLN 5,000-15,000 onboarding and PLN 750-2,500 per month based on services, subcontractors, and active customer rooms
economics.retention_or_repeat: Evidence, subcontractors, services, and customer renewals change continuously, supporting annual retention if multiple buyers reuse the record

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: A reusable mapping between supplier facts, service relationships, contract clauses, evidence documents, and the structured register fields requested across many financial entities
fingerprint.customer: Small cloud, analytics, cybersecurity, and software vendors already selling or trying to sell to EU insurers, payment firms, asset managers, credit institutions, and other DORA-covered entities
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: ISO auditors, financial-compliance advisers, MSPs, and cloud marketplaces refer vendors at the point a regulated customer requests evidence
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: A canonical vendor-and-service evidence graph with signed source documents, subcontractor chains, DORA register exports, reusable answers, and contract-clause gap flags; paid setup plus annual subscription
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: The ICT vendor pays at the first regulated-customer diligence request, then subscribes per service and active customer evidence room
fingerprint.problem_trigger: Since 17 January 2025, covered financial entities must maintain comprehensive registers of ICT third-party contracts, assess providers before contracting, and monitor third-party risk, repeatedly pulling structured facts and evidence from vendors

founder_fit: Relational supplier graphs and data-quality checks match the founder's analytical background
Finance interest helps with buyer vocabulary without requiring regulated investment activity
The vendor-side wedge supports self-serve onboarding and asynchronous evidence exchange
Auditor and adviser channels reduce constant enterprise networking
risks: The platform would store highly sensitive security and subcontractor evidence.
Incorrect contract-clause guidance could delay or damage a procurement decision.
Network value will not compound if each bank insists on incompatible evidence formats.
Sales may remain consultant-led and meeting-heavy despite the intended channel model.

structure.commercial_archetype: Supplier-side procurement passport and evidence-room subscription
structure.control_point: The reusable service-and-subcontractor record presented before a regulated financial customer approves or renews an ICT vendor
structure.critical_dependency: Acceptance of exports and source-linked evidence by financial buyers that remain legally responsible for their own due diligence

thesis: A supplier-side DORA evidence passport can let small ICT vendors maintain one structured record of services, entities, subcontractors, controls, contracts, and evidence links, then export customer-specific rooms for regulated financial buyers. DORA puts the legal duty on financial entities, but that duty becomes a procurement constraint for their suppliers; the product wins only if it removes repeated questionnaires without asking banks to abandon their own systems.
title: DORA Supplier Evidence Passport for Finance-Facing ICT Vendors
uncertainties: No evidence yet shows regulated buyers will accept a portable evidence room as reducing their workload.
The target vendor count, questionnaire frequency, and renewal churn are unmeasured.
The proposed pricing and 1,200-vendor wealth scenario are unvalidated assumptions.
Which DORA fields can be vendor-authored versus financial-entity-authored needs precise mapping.
